articles.title: 'Não houve conflito nem briga', diz assessoria sobre Virginia e Vini | G1
articles.standfirst: Influenciadora e jogador de futebol confirmaram fim do relacionamento neste domingo (11). Assessoria disse que houve apenas o "entendimento de não seguirem mais como um casal".
articles.summary: Influenciadora e jogador de futebol confirmaram fim do relacionamento neste domingo (11). Assessoria disse que houve apenas o "entendimento de não seguirem mais como um casal".
articles.body:
A assessoria de imprensa da influenciadora Virginia Fonseca informou, neste domingo (11), que "não houve conflito nem briga" no término do relacionamento entre ela e o jogador Vini Jr . A assessoria disse que houve apenas o "entendimento de não seguirem mais como um casal".

Nos últimos dias, cresceram os rumores nas redes sociais sobre um possível fim do namoro. Nem Virginia nem Vini publicaram nada sobre o assunto até o momento, em seus perfis.

Virginia Fonseca e Vini Jr: assessoria de imprensa da influenciadora confirmou o término do relacionamento — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram Virginia e Vini Jr.

A relação entre os dois, que teve início em outubro de 2025 , foi marcada por idas e vindas. Em maio deste ano, a influenciadora fez um desabafo nas redes, dizendo que havia terminado a relação e que se dedicou muito ao namoro dos dois, mas que aprendeu a "nunca negociar aquilo que é inegociável".

"Enquanto estivemos juntos, me dediquei muito, como me dedico a tudo o que me proponho a viver na minha vida. [...] Ao longo da minha vida, aprendi a nunca negociar aquilo que, pra mim, é inegociável. Então, quando algo deixa de fazer sentido, eu prefiro ter maturidade para encerrar com carinho, do que permanecer por permanecer", disse a influenciadora, na ocasião.

Em julho, o casal apareceu junto novamente, durante inauguração da academia de Virginia , em Goiânia . Ambos confirmaram que haviam se reconciliado .

As aparições públicas eram uma rotina deles. No mesmo mês em que reataram, os dois apareceram juntos na festa de aniversário de 3 anos do afilhado da empresária, na capital goiana. No evento, o jogador apareceu em um vídeo brincando com José Leonardo, o caçula de Virginia .

Os dois também costumavam compartilhar momentos românticos nas redes sociais. Quando estavam completando apenas um mês de namoro, Virginia ganhou do jogador um buquê de rosas gigante .

Na ocasião, Virginia falou sobre a surpresa logo cedo: “Hoje acordei sendo mimada pelo meu amor!”. Por sua vez, o jogador do Real Madrid comentou na publicação validando o romance: “Te amo, e que seja o primeiro de muitos”, disse.

articles.title: El Andorra vuelve a ganar en el Principado y endosa la primera derrota al Castellón
articles.standfirst: Un gol de Sidibe en la primera parte fue suficiente para que el Andorra sumara tres puntos
articles.summary: Un gol de Sidibe en la primera parte fue suficiente para que el Andorra sumara tres puntos
articles.body: El Andorra ha dado un golpe sobre la mesa al imponerse por la mínima al Castellón y acabar con la condición de invicto de los de Pablo Hernández. Los tricolores, que llegaban reforzados tras sumar cuatro de los últimos seis puntos a domicilio, han encontrado el premio a su buen arranque con un tanto de Moró Sidibe y han sabido resistir la reacción visitante en una segunda mitad de mayor sufrimiento. Con una versión más pragmática, pero sin renunciar a su identidad, los de Carles Manso han conseguido además saldar su deuda pendiente con la afición y volver a celebrar un triunfo como locales. Los pupilos de Gerard Piqué han llevado el ritmo del partido y Efe Akman ha abierto la lata muy temprano, aunque el tanto ha terminado anulado por fuera de juego de Sidibe, su asistente. El susto ha dejado tocado los 'orelluts', que han intentado despejarse con una presión alta y les ha salido en contra, pues los locales lo han aprovechado para golpear en largo con Jordi Cano, quien ha llegado hasta la línea de fondo y se la ha regalado a Sidibe dentro del área. Esta vez el tanto sí que ha subido al luminoso y el golpe ha sido más duro para los de Pablo Hernández, que a punto han estado de encajar el segundo a la salida de un córner. Así, los pirenaicos se lo han pasado en grande sobre el verde, cuando en el ecuador de la primera mitad se ha ralentizado el tempo y, a medida que corría, los castellonenses se iban encontrando más cómodos. Aunque de poco ha servido para ver otra acción de peligro más allá de una para cada conjunto. La segunda mitad ha dado inicio con el Castellón acechando portería contraria, pero pronto los del país vecino han vuelto a hacerse con la esférica para hacer daño con balones al espacio. Tras un aviso de Diego Alende, el juego de ambos ha pasado a ser en largo, con los visitantes como dominadores y una de muy clara para cada uno. La primera ha sido para Iñigo Córdoba con un latigazo de fuera del área que Jesús Owono ha rechazado con una gran mano cuando el balón estaba por colarse por la escuadra; y la segunda para Thomas Carrique, perdonando el mano a mano y teniendo compañeros esperando el pase. Si bien ha continuado mandando el equipo albinegro, los dos conjuntos han tenido ocasiones claras de sobra para mover un marcador que se ha mantenido con el 1-0 hasta el pitido final.

articles.title: Giráldez: "Había mucha gente mareada al acabar el partido, mucho calor para estas alturas del año"
articles.standfirst: “El nivel del día de hoy no me llega”, dijo el técnico, que no estaba satisfecho el desempeño de su equipo
articles.summary: “El nivel del día de hoy no me llega”, dijo el técnico, que no estaba satisfecho el desempeño de su equipo
articles.body: No estaba satisfecho Claudio Giráldez con el encuentro de su equipo en Elche, en el que hubo varios aspectos que no le gustaron. Valoración del encuentro: “Un partido con muy pocas ocasiones de gol, un rival que ha sido superior. Ninguno de los dos equipos ha sido capaz de robarle la pelota al otro. La diferencia es que ellos no se han deshecho del balón, lo han cuidado, y nosotros lo hemos tirado. Hemos tenido una o dos ocasiones de Driouech para llevarnos los tres puntos, pero no hubiese sido justo”. Más análisis: "Hemos sido peores que el rival. Ellos han interpretado mejor el día de calor asfixiante que hacía. Es un partido con pocas ocasiones. En un día en el que no estás bien con o sin balón, que no te hagan gol, puede ser una lectura positiva, pero yo no me voy contento con el equipo. Mucha gente mareada al acabar el partido, mucho calor para estas alturas del año". Optimista: “La lectura positiva es que un día en el que no hemos estado cómodos, que hemos sufrido y no hemos jugado de nuestra forma habitual, nos vamos con portería a cero y cinco partidos seguidos sin perder en LaLiga y con un punto que a lo largo del año esperamos que se agradezca”. Sobre los cuatro empates como visitantes, tres de ellos sin goles: “Dice que no estamos atacando bien, pero sí lo estamos haciendo bien defendiendo fuera de casa”. No le gustó su equipo: “El nivel del día de hoy no me llega, es una realidad. No me ha gustado. Nos hemos precipitado en muchos ataques, hemos estado imprecisos en lo técnico, hemos llegado tarde a la presión. Tenemos que hacer mucho más para ganar, pero tenemos una base sólida que nos permite competir”.

articles.title: Cardoso y Vargas, en la lista de convocados para visitar al Levante
articles.standfirst: El Sevilla cita a 24 jugadores para el Ciutat de València, entre los que destacan los regresos del portugués y el suizo
articles.summary: El Sevilla cita a 24 jugadores para el Ciutat de València, entre los que destacan los regresos del portugués y el suizo
articles.body: El Sevilla ha publicado la lista de convocados para viajar hacia Valencia, donde el lunes se medirá al Levante en el duelo que cerrará la octava jornada de LaLiga EA Sports (21:00 horas). Luis García Plaza ha decidido llevarse a 24 futbolistas en la expedición hispalense, por lo que deberá realizar un descarte a última hora. Las grandes novedades de la lista son Fábio Cardoso y Rubén Vargas. El luso, que estuvo toda la pretemporada entrenando al margen mientras se le buscaba salida, no contaba para García Plaza, pero las bajas en el eje de la zaga, donde siguen lesionados Marcao e Iker Muñoz, propician su primera convocatoria del curso. Por su parte, el suizo regresa después de siete jornadas, ya que hasta ahora solo había participado en la jornada inaugural. Kike Salas repite su presencia en la lista. Pese a que el canterano ya fue citado para jugar contra el Barcelona, el cuerpo técnico quiso evitar riesgos y optó por descartarlo. Respecto a aquel encuentro, además de Marcao e Iker Muñoz, también se caen Nico Guillén y Rafa Romero, que deja su lugar a Loren. Tampoco estará finalmente Lucas Stassin, que aún continúa con su puesta a punto y no ha podido entrenar con el grupo. La lista completa del Sevilla está compuesta por Vlachodimos, Fran González, Loren, Juan Iglesias, Carmona, Kike Salas, Fábio Cardoso, Andrés Castrín, Sangante, Gabriel Suazo, Julio Díaz, Agoumé, Fofana, Kochorashvili, Manu Bueno, Guridi, Alfon, Vargas, Félix Correia, Miguel Sierra, Ejuke, Peque, Robbie Ure e Isaac Romero.

articles.title: Fichar a Haaland por 60 millones sí que fue 'ilegal'
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Liverpool - Manchester City
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Liverpool - Manchester City
articles.body: Con el pelo largo o corto... no hay delantero en el mundo como Erling Haaland. Con el partido atascado y camino del 0-0 en el duelo más esperado post-parón de selecciones, el noruego apareció para quebrar por completo Anfield con un tanto de auténtico '9'. Olió la oportunidad tras la roja de Gravenberch e hizo sangre. 170 goles en 206 partidos vestido de 'sky blue', el noveno que le hace al Liverpool, una de sus víctimas favoritas. Fichar al vikingo por 'solamente' 60 millones en 2022 sí que fue 'ilegal'. Su padre mientras, lo celebraba en la grada. A la espera del resultado de la apelación y un veredicto final (con sanción o no), Haaland encumbra al City al liderato. El ambiente fue el esperado para el primer partido post declaración de culpabilidad del Manchester City. Mas aún, con lo caprichoso que había sido el calendario: los 'sky blues' viajaban a Anfield, la casa del que ha sido su gran rival esta última década. La hinchada 'Red' recibió a los de Maresca con pancartas de todo tipo (en las gradas y fuera del estadio), con merchandising que reflejaba las "trampas" del City a la venta en los puestos de los aledaños... y con una sonora pitada antes del inicio del duelo. El City, sin embargo, 'surfeó' bien la presión y lo que se impuso en Anfield fue el 'banana gate' de la hinchada visitante. Pagar una 'millonada' por un futbolista hoy día ya no es sinónimo de éxito. Que se lo digan al Liverpool. Los de Anfield invirtieron 125 millones en Florian Wirtz y otros tantos en Bradley Barcola... y a ambos se les sigue esperando. Más 'delito' tiene lo del alemán, pues el galo acaba de llegar a Inglaterra, pero la sensación es clara: sobrepagar por un fichaje en el fútbol inglés sale muy barato. Del Klopp vs Guardiola al Iraola vs Maresca. El de este domingo en Anfield fue el primer partido de la Premier League entre el Liverpool y el Man City sin Jurgen Klopp ni Pep Guardiola en el banquillo... desde marzo de 2015, cuando los 'Reds' de Brendan Rodgers vencieron al City de Manuel Pellegrini por 2-1. Un cambio de 'era' en uno de los duelos que ha marcado la Premier en los últimos años. Como reconoció Guardiola en numerosas ocasiones, Klopp fue su mayor rival. Maresca, mientras, hace historia: 18 puntos de 18 posibles en las primeras seis jornadas igualando el mejor registro de siempre en el club... marcado por Pep Guardiola en la 2016-17 y 2023-24. 23 partidos, mientras, era la cantidad de partidos que llevaba sin perder Iraola en liga inglesa. 18 con el Bournemouth y cinco con el 'Pool'. Su Liverpool no 'arranca'.

articles.title: Maresca: "¿Críticas? Tenemos que afrontar esto y hacer nuestro propio ruido"
articles.standfirst: El técnico italiano habló tras el triunfo del City en Anfield
articles.summary: El técnico italiano habló tras el triunfo del City en Anfield
articles.body: Un 0-3 contundente en Anfield que dejó radiante a Enzo Maresca. El técnico italiano del City igualó el mejor arranque de la 'era Guardiola' con 18 puntos de 18 posibles. Los 'sky blues' son líderes en solitario mientras se decide qué pasará con su futuro, si habrá sanción o no... pero, por ahora, responden en el césped. Maresca, mientras, habló tras el partido. El contexto y el partido. "Circunstancias muy difíciles, un ambiente complicado. Tuvimos problemas en la primera parte; teníamos el balón, pero no lo hacíamos bien sin él. En la segunda parte hicimos algunos ajustes y mejoramos mucho. En la construcción del juego no estábamos haciendo las cosas bien, pero en la segunda parte mejoramos". El ambiente en Anfield. "Tenemos que aprender a lidiar con el ruido porque estará presente en todos nuestros partidos fuera de casa; habrá ruido. Tenemos que afrontarlo y hacer nuestro propio ruido. Nuestro ruido es para ganar partidos. La sensación al final del partido con nuestros aficionados y nuestro ruido es una sensación agradable y un ruido diferente". ¿Ambiente más intenso de lo habitual?. "No lo sé con exactitud, ya vine aquí con el City una vez, en la temporada del triplete. Fue agradable jugar este tipo de partido por el ruido, el ambiente... Tenemos que hacer nuestro ruido y lidiar con el suyo". Sobre si los problemas extradeportivos pueden motivar al equipo. "Probablemente sí, probablemente no. No lo sé. Puede crear unión con la afición. Durante la semana dije que pusiéramos pasión, que hiciéramos ruido y que, con suerte, podríamos celebrar una victoria. Es lo único en lo que podemos centrarnos".

articles.title: After new Abu Dhabi property purchase, Erling Haaland could now unlock UAE’s coveted 10-year Golden Visa via two different pathways
articles.summary: Erling Haaland's investment in Abu Dhabi property may qualify him for a 10-year UAE Golden Visa, available through property investment or recognition for his athletic achievements. This article explores the implications of his move and the potential pathways to UAE residency.
articles.body: Erling Haaland’s new home in Abu Dhabi puts the Manchester City striker in a position where securing a 10-year UAE Golden Visa could be a straightforward step if he chooses to pursue it. Given his status as one of football’s biggest stars, his achievements on the pitch and his ties to an Abu Dhabi-backed club, he could also be considered for a Golden Visa through special recognition rather than relying solely on the property investment route. While there has been no official announcement that Haaland has been granted the visa, his profile makes him a natural candidate for such an opportunity. However, he has not publicly expressed any intention or ambition to pursue UAE residency.Haaland’s new Abu Dhabi home puts a 10-year visa within reachHaaland announced his property purchase today through a video shared by the developers, revealing that he and his father, former Manchester City player Alf-Inge Haaland, had bought homes in the Manchester City Ohana project in Abu Dhabi. The development, created in collaboration with real estate company Ohana Residences, brings the club’s branding into a luxury waterfront community on Yas Island.“Hi everyone, I’m so happy because I’m joining the Manchester City Ohana project. We will be neighbours in Abu Dhabi…I just got a house and so did my father,” Haaland said at the project’s launch event at the Etihad Arena.The development offers townhouses, duplexes, and villas with prices starting above AED 3,600,000 ($1.02 million) for an average two-bedroom townhouse. A five-bedroom waterfront villa is expected to cost approximately $2.91 million, while bespoke estates reportedly start at $9.95 million.The project also includes a Manchester City Training Academy, a City Lounge, and recreational facilities, while more than half of its master plan is dedicated to green spaces. Haaland’s exact property and purchase price have not been disclosed, but the development’s reported price range puts its residences above the UAE’s AED 2 million ($544,500) property-investment threshold.The property naturally open the door to long-term residency in the UAE, adding another potential benefit to Haaland’s latest investment. Whether a Golden Visa forms part of the package or something he chooses to pursue separately, his new Abu Dhabi home adds to his growing ties to the country.What the UAE Golden Visa offers beyond a property purchaseThe Golden Visa is a long-term UAE residency programme designed to attract investors, entrepreneurs, skilled professionals, and people with exceptional talent. Under the current federal programme, eligible applicants can obtain renewable residency for 10 years without requiring a local sponsor, giving them greater independence from the employer-linked arrangements associated with conventional residency permits.The programme allows qualifying residents to live, work, study and invest in the UAE, while extending residency opportunities to their families. Its main benefits include:Long-term residency: A renewable 10-year permit provides greater continuity than shorter-term residence arrangements.Family sponsorship: Holders can obtain residence permits for their spouses, children regardless of age and parents, as well as sponsor domestic workers under applicable regulations.Greater independence: Residents do not need an employer or another local sponsor to maintain their Golden Visa status.Flexible travel: Holders can remain outside the UAE for longer than the usual six-month absence limit that applies to many other residence visas.An entry period for overseas applicants: Eligible applicants outside the country can receive a six-month multiple-entry visa, renewable for another six months, while completing their residency procedures.The programme serves several different categories, including property investors, entrepreneurs, scientists, outstanding students, and exceptional talents. Each pathway has its own eligibility rules, meaning applicants do not necessarily need to purchase expensive real estate to obtain long-term residency.How Haaland’s property purchase could qualify himAbu Dhabi’s official guidance for real estate investors sets a minimum qualifying property value of AED 2 million ($544,500), with ownership and investment documentation required as part of the application. Applicants may combine eligible properties to reach the threshold, while mortgages through national banks can be accepted when the investor’s qualifying capital remains at least AED 2 million ($544,500).The requirements also distinguish between completed properties and off-plan purchases, which is particularly relevant for a newly launched development such as Manchester City Ohana Residences. For off-plan property, the applicant must provide a purchase agreement from an approved developer and evidence that at least AED 2 million ($544,500) has already been paid towards the property.Although the development’s homes would qualify buyers for a 10-year Golden Visa, Haaland’s exact unit, payment arrangements and application status remain undisclosed, largely because the project is still being developed.For Haaland, the property-investment route is the obvious starting point following his Abu Dhabi purchase. However, even without his new home, the UAE has an established traditional pathway for athletes to obtain a Golden Visa, meaning his achievements and standing in football could provide another route to long-term residency should he wish to pursue it.The athlete pathway could make the property investment unnecessaryAbu Dhabi’s Golden Visa programme includes a 10-year residency category for athletes under its broader provision for outstanding talent. The official criteria focus on exceptional sporting ability and achievements, while the application process requires evidence that supports the applicant’s standing in their field.An athlete applying through Abu Dhabi’s published route must provide:A sporting résumé documenting achievements and experience in their discipline.Supporting certificates or experience letters confirming those sporting accomplishments.A recommendation from Abu Dhabi Sports Council, which is the key formal endorsement in the published process.Applications submitted through the Abu Dhabi Residents Office’s online system are automatically forwarded to the sports council for nomination, while applicants can also submit through the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security.However, Haaland may not need to go through the usual nomination process to make a compelling case. As one of the most feared strikers of his generation and a global football superstar with a larger-than-life profile, his credentials speak for themselves. Should he wish to pursue the athlete route, his record would be difficult to overlook. To put that into context, Haaland could point to his Champions League triumph, multiple Premier League Golden Boot awards and standing among the world's elite footballers as evidence of his sporting achievements.Crucially, the UAE's published athlete pathway does not require the AED 2 million ($544,500) property investment threshold. Eligible athletes can instead seek residency based on their sporting credentials, subject to the relevant authority's assessment and approval. Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi connection adds another dimensionHaaland’s situation is particularly interesting given Manchester City’s deep-rooted ties to Abu Dhabi. The club’s majority owner, Newton Investment and Development LLC, is wholly owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE’s Vice-President and Deputy Prime Minister. Since the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008, City’s relationship with the emirate has grown considerably, and the partnership with Ohana Residences has now brought that connection into the property market.Haaland is no ordinary player in this arrangement. As one of Manchester City’s biggest stars and the face of a development carrying the club’s name, he occupies a position of enormous commercial value. It is easy to see why his new home could be viewed as more than a property purchase, particularly given the UAE’s interest in attracting some of the biggest names in global sport and entertainment. One could even imagine a purchase of this nature being accompanied by residency arrangements, although no such package has been publicly confirmed in Haaland’s case.Over the years, the UAE has attracted and welcomed prominent athletes, sporting personalities, actors, scientists and other internationally recognised figures, offering long-term residency opportunities to people whose achievements and expertise align with its ambitions. Against that backdrop, Haaland would have an exceptionally compelling case to present. His Champions League success, Premier League Golden Boot awards and status as one of the most recognisable footballers of his generation would make him a standout candidate under the country's athlete pathway.Whether through his Abu Dhabi property or recognition of his sporting achievements, Haaland has a strong basis to explore long-term UAE residency should he wish to do so. articles.title: CFP Playoff Bracket, Scenarios and Bowl Projections After 2026-27 Week 7 AP Rankings
articles.summary: The Georgia Bulldogs are the new top team in the AP Top 25.
articles.body:
The Georgia Bulldogs are the new top team in the AP Top 25.

Georgia's win over the Alabama Crimson Tide combined with the Texas Longhorns' defeat to the Oklahoma Sooners caused the shift at the top of the Week 7 rankings.

The 6-0 Bulldogs are on top for now, but they still have a tricky SEC schedule to navigate in order to confirm a spot in the College Football Playoff.

Due to Texas' loss, Georgia is the only SEC team in the top five. The Notre Dame Fighting Irish, Miami Hurricanes, Ohio State Buckeyes and Indiana Hoosiers fill out the top five in that order.

Ohio State and Indiana will play for the top spot in the Big Ten in Week 7. That's one of two top-10 matchups to look forward to on Saturday as well as Notre Dame's battle with the BYU Cougars.

Georgia Sits On Top For First Time This Season

Georgia moved up one spot from No. 2 to claim its first week atop the AP poll.

Gunner Stockton and Co. went into Tuscaloosa to pick up their first big win of the 2026 campaign.

As of now, Georgia has the chance to pick up two more Top 25 wins in SEC play against the No. 9 Ole Miss Rebels and the No. 13 Missouri Tigers.

UGA's schedule looks easier than the upcoming run of games for the likes of Texas and Ohio State.

The schedule and the way Georgia handled its win at Alabama suggest the Bulldogs should be the favorite to claim one of the four first-round byes in the CFB Playoff.

A spot in the SEC Championship Game is the minimum expectation, but it would come as no surprise to see UGA on the finalized top four seed lines come December.

Arch Manning and Texas tumbled down to No. 7 following their last-second loss to Oklahoma.

Texas was unable to squeeze out another close win, like it did against Ohio State and Tennessee.

Texas is 4-1 with a pair of top-15 wins, but there has to be at least a slight bit of concern about the Longhorns' playoff hopes.

Steve Sarkisian's team plays Florida, Ole Miss, Mississippi State, Missouri and LSU in its next five games.

The first three of those games take place in Austin, which should aid Texas' chances of getting through October with one loss.

Texas is capable of going 5-0 or 4-1 in that stretch and preserving a spot in the CFB Playoff, and potentially the SEC Championship Game.

The Longhorns can't afford two losses in that stretch, though, because getting in as a three-loss team, even from the SEC, could be tough.

Stage Set For Two Top 10 Clashes in Week 7

Two top-10 clashes in Week 7 will have significant CFB Playoff ramifications.

The first of the two takes place in Bloomington, as Ohio State fights Indiana for Big Ten supremacy.

Ohio State and Indiana are two of four Big Ten teams left without a loss in league play. Indiana and the UCLA Bruins are the only programs with full undefeated records in the Big Ten.

The OSU-Indiana winner will be a front-runner to land a first-round bye in the CFB Playoff.

If Ohio State loses, it then puts its playoff life on thin ice because it would then have to defeats to Texas and Indiana.

Notre Dame's trip to BYU is likely more about the Cougars' playoff prospects.

The Fighting Irish have been a machine through six games. They have six double-digit wins and have scored at least 37 points in five of their six contests.

BYU sits on top of the Big 12, but it hasn't faced a ranked opponent yet in five games.

The Cougars are one of three playoff contenders in the Big 12, along with Texas Tech and Utah.

If BYU pulls off the win at home, it has a case to be a top-five team, and it will significantly shake up the rankings.

After six weeks, the assumption is Notre Dame will join Georgia, Miami and the Big Ten champion as the four teams with first-round byes.

articles.title: Pellegrini: "Tras un parón de tres semanas era importantísimo volver con una victoria"
articles.standfirst: El Ingeniero califica como "completísimo" el partido de su equipo frente a Osasuna
articles.summary: El Ingeniero califica como "completísimo" el partido de su equipo frente a Osasuna
articles.body: Manuel Pellegrini, técnico del Betis, se mostró satisfecho con el triunfo de su equipo ante Osasuna, restó importancia a las quejas de los rojillos que pidieron expulsión de Natan en la acción inmediatamente interior al gol con el que Isco ponía el 4-2 en el marcador y evitó lanzar las campanas al vuelo por el gran arranque de temporada de su equipo, centrándose desde ya en el duelo de Champions ante el Oporto del próximo miércoles. Un partido que parecía controlado: "El fútbol nunca está controlado. Los resultados indican una superioridad a un equipo, pero en cuanto se baja un poco el ritmo el otro equipo lo puede igualar. Son acciones puntuales que igualan todo lo que es un trabajo colectivo, pero creo que el equipo hizo un muy buen partido, completísimo. En el primer tiempo prácticamente no nos llegaron a portería, nos pusimos 2-0, tuvimos una importante en el primer gol que los metió a ellos en el 3 a 1, después se sintieron también más cerca con el 3 a 2, pero retomamos la llegada y marcamos cinco goles". Objetivo, los puestos Champions: "Yo creo que el único objetivo que tenemos que tener es tratar de ganar el miércoles en la Champions aquí. Una vez que terminemos la Champions, nos meteremos en el partido siguiente. Estamos insertos en tres competiciones, entonces vamos a intentar hacerlo lo mejor posible en las tres. Es muy importante mantener una regularidad, por eso que después de este parón habíamos comenzado muy bien el campeonato, pero tras un parón de tres semanas era importantísimo volver con una victoria y jugando con el nivel que jugó el equipo". El nivel de Isco: "Bueno, yo me alegro mucho por él porque lo ha pasado muy mal. Ha tenido dos lesiones, además de fracturas bastante inéditas para un jugador que no es de lesiones; tampoco fueron musculares, fueron fracturas, entonces lo ha pasado mal, pero tiene una calidad espectacular y una madurez como jugador que le permite rendir al nivel que quiera. Pero además de Isco, yo creo que también hay un espíritu de equipo en el que trabajamos todos por recuperar y después con el balón todos por intentar jugar". Polémica en el cuarto gol: "Bueno, lo vi en el banquillo y lo vi ahora en la televisión. Son manotazos, entran los dos con las manos, no era ni el impulso de la mano de Natan para tirarse de esa manera al piso. Así que no me pareció ningún error del árbitro porque de esas jugadas hay en todos los partidos". El estreno liguero de Morante: "Bueno, a Morante lo estamos llevando desde la temporada pasada. Ya jugó en la Copa del Rey, entrena normalmente en las pretemporadas con el equipo y ahora está entrenando también con el primer equipo, aunque baja a jugar al filial. Yo creo que es un jugador que tiene mucho futuro, que todavía tiene que mejorar mucho y se mejora justamente trabajando todos los días con los Isco, con los Lo Celso, con los Fornals, con toda la gente de experiencia y calidad que tiene este plantel. Así que me alegro mucho por él de que haya convertido un gol; no es una casualidad porque le pega muy bien al balón, así que es una alternativa más para el plantel en el que tenemos muchísimos partidos".

articles.title: Rubén García: "No se puede permitir encajar cinco goles"
articles.standfirst: El capitán rojillo quiso hacer autocrítica tras la goleada sufrida ante el Betis
articles.summary: El capitán rojillo quiso hacer autocrítica tras la goleada sufrida ante el Betis
articles.body: El extremo de Osasuna Rubén García asumió que "es importante ver qué está pasando" para que el equipo navarro atraviese esta serie de resultados negativos y muestre la "debilidad" que lo ha llevado a "encajar cinco goles" en el campo del Betis, algo que "no se puede permitir". "Nos está costando. Sin excusas en la primera parte, eso es lo primero. En la acción previa al 4-2, noto contacto con su rodilla en mi pierna y sin querer me tira. El árbitro me dice que no es suficiente. Podemos hablar de mil cosas, pero debemos asumir la responsabilidad y de esta derrota y no podemos estar orgullosos", ha señalado el jugador valenciano sobre una decisión arbitral con el partido aún con el 3-2. Rubén García, en declaraciones a Movistar, ha asegurado que "el fútbol tiene cosas que son difíciles de explicar" porque "en la primera parte, dos errores" dan al traste con "la idea" de su equipo de esperar al Betis "en bloque bajo y salir a la contra, pero no ha servido" a la vista del 2-0 que campeaba en el marcador al descanso. El capitán rojillo cree que "se van los partidos quizá por falta de hambre o de ambición", algo que el plantel ha "intentado trabajar, pero no ha servido para hoy" debido también a "acciones puntuales" del arbitraje "que a veces caen en contra", si bien ha resaltado que los colegiados "lo hacen lo mejor posible".

articles.title: Winless and an 'easy touch' - what's happened to the Anfield fear factor?
articles.summary: Liverpool's struggles at Anfield continue as Iraola still awaits his first Premier League win at Anfield.
articles.body:
It is early days but Andoni Iraola will know that if his time at Liverpool is going to be a success, then he must make Anfield a fortress again.

Liverpool were impressive for the most part against a Manchester City side that arrived on Merseyside with a 100% record.

However, once Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in the 62nd minute, they capitulated to a 3-0 defeat.

As Iraola said post-match to Match of the Day: "We played two different games. One until the red card, and then after.

"For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us."

His unbeaten start is now over. This was actually his first Premier League defeat in 24 games (W10, D13) since January, including his time at Bournemouth .

The Reds, though, are now winless in three Premier League home matches this season - although they have won at Anfield in the Champions League and Carabao Cup - for just the second time ever.

That winless run in the league at Anfield stretches back to last season with Liverpool now winless in five successive Premier League home games (D4 L1).

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock told BBC Radio 5 Live: "The best teams in the world are also horrible to play against. Liverpool aren't horrible.

"They're an easy touch at the moment. They have too many players that are nice and they have to change that part of things.

" Liverpool have got a lot of work to do.

"They don't have enough leaders at the moment, apart from Virgil van Dijk barking orders."

'Man City's Anfield win has feeling of irrelevance with season in limbo'

Man City cruise to statement win over 10-man Liverpool

Going back to the start of the year, Liverpool have won just four games in 13 Anfield Premier League matches.

In fact, they have won more matches away from home than at home during this period.

A closer look at the stats clearly shows Liverpool 's home form has dropped off season by season since 2023-2024, although it is important to note this season is still a very small sample size.

Away sides have a lower win percentage at Anfield (12.5 per cent) than at any other stadium in Premier League history.

However, is this reputation starting to dwindle?

Ex-Man Utd midfielder Paul Scholes told The Good, the Bad and the Football podcast in September: "When you go to Liverpool , especially when Jurgen Klopp was there, the crowd played such a major part. It feels like that's gone… I don't think the fans are quite on board at the minute with what's happening there.

"When we used to go there, I'd think, 'how are we going to get the ball?', because they were on top of you. Teams seem to have a lot more possession and look a bit more comfortable than they ever have."

And Scholes' former team-mate Nicky Butt added: "The likes of Fulham five years ago are going to Anfield and they're beaten before they even go up the steps."

City's class highlights Liverpool's concerns

While Liverpool have won twice on their travels this season, they now sit ninth in the league - and their main issue seems fairly clear.

They have scored just seven goals this season - just twice at Anfield - and only seven teams have managed fewer.

It was early on in the first half when the cameras panned to Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai in the Main Stand at Anfield - all three of them were out with injuries.

Among them, the trio have scored six of Liverpool 's seven league goals this season and on a day when Man City's attack showed their class, Liverpool didn't show any quality in the final third.

City (16) have scored more than double the goals Liverpool (7) have scored this season in the top flight.

Across three league games at Anfield this season, Liverpool have failed to score in two of them. That must improve.

In Isak's absence, Lewis Koumas put in a great shift. However, the 21-year-old lacks that killer edge in front of goal at this level.

The focus must fall on Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. It is this kind of game where you need a match-winning moment and neither showed anywhere near the quality that is expected when you have a price tag of over £100m.

There was one moment at 0-0 in the 55th minute when Wirtz had Milos Kerkez and Barcola in acres of space to his left, but chose to shoot and fired wide.

"You learn a lot in games like today," Iraola said. "I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It's a loss and we didn't get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot."

But deep down, Iraola will know there is a lot of work to do and getting the big money signings to deliver will be high on his agenda.

articles.title: Kentucky Fined for Fans Storming Field After Upset Win vs. Lane Kiffin's LSU, Tigers to Get $500K
articles.summary: Kentucky extended its winning streak to five with a thrilling 35-34 overtime victory over LSU on Saturday, but it ended up being a costly result for the program.
articles.body:
Kentucky extended its winning streak to five with a thrilling 35-34 overtime victory over LSU on Saturday, but it ended up being a costly result for the program.

David Ubben of The Athletic reported Sunday the SEC fined Kentucky $500,000 because its fans stormed the field following the upset of Lane Kiffin's squad. The conference changed its "access to competition area" rule last year, which means the fine will go directly to the Tigers.

The SEC first started fining programs for storming the field in 2004 but changed the rule in 2025 to make the penalty $500,000 regardless of the sport and whether there were multiple offenses.

"The motivation was 'field rushing is field rushing, the first time or the 18th time,'" SEC commissioner Greg Sankey said, per Ubben.

While the Wildcats were punished, it likely does little to dampen spirits in Kentucky following such a dramatic win. Despite missing two field goals earlier in the game, Adam Zouagui connected on a kick in the final seconds of regulation to send the game to overtime.

From there, LSU scored a touchdown first when Sam Leavitt ran it in from 15 yards out to give the visitors the lead. However, Kentucky responded right back when CJ Baxter found the end zone on a one-yard run.

Rather than kick the extra point and go into a second overtime, the Wildcats decided to go for two. And quarterback Kenny Minchey took advantage of the opportunity when he kept it on a draw play and scored for the conversion.

It was the second consecutive week Kentucky went for two after a touchdown in overtime to win the game by the exact score of 35-34. It did so against South Carolina as well, and Minchey found Willie Rodriguez for the two-point conversion to win it that time.

The Wildcats are now 5-1 overall and 3-1 in the SEC following the last two wins. While they still have road games against Tennessee, Oklahoma and Missouri, as well as home games against Florida and Louisville, they are in position to compete for the College Football Playoff as the season progresses.

Of course, that may lead to some more field storming as well.

articles.title: Morante se estrena a lo grande
articles.standfirst: El canterano había jugado ya minutos en la UEFA Europa League, pero marcó un golazo en su debut en LaLiga
articles.summary: El canterano había jugado ya minutos en la UEFA Europa League, pero marcó un golazo en su debut en LaLiga
articles.body: Debutó con el primer equipo en partido oficial en enero, ante el PAOK en la Europa League. Pero ayer, después de integrarse ya en la dinámica habitual de trabajo a las órdenes de Pellegrini, Morante tuvo la oportunidad de estrenarse en LaLiga, en La Cartuja. Y lo hizo de la mejor manera posible, con un golazo en el tiempo añadido que celebró toreando, como su padre. El canterano recibió entre líneas y no se lo pensó: zurdazo que tras rozar en un defensa sorprendió a Aitor Fernández. La primera tarde de un futbolista que brilla en las selecciones inferiores y que está llamado a convertirse en una estrella en el Betis. Pellegrini mima los pasos de su carrera. "Morante lo estamos llevando desde la temporada pasada, ya jugó la Copa del Rey. Entrena con el equipo, juega con el filial. Le queda mucho por aprender pero con los Isco y compañía le vendrá bien. El gol no es casualidad porque le pega muy bien al balón", dijo el entrenador chileno.

articles.title: Manchester City: A statement win but does it carry weight in a season of limbo?
articles.summary: Manchester City record what they will view as a statement win at Liverpool - but is it a statement that carries any weight during a Premier League season in limbo, asks Phil McNulty?
articles.body:
Manchester City made what they will regard as a powerful statement in the most hostile territory against Liverpool at Anfield - but is it a statement that carries any weight during a Premier League season in limbo?

City's attention turned to on-field matters in their first game since being found guilty of 114 charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

The fates, and fixture list, decreed it would be at Liverpool , whose fans nurse the most burning sense of injustice after finishing second to City in 2013-14, 2018-19 and 2021-22.

Their argument centres on the belief those titles could have been theirs had City not possessed the high finance of their Abu Dhabi-based owners, using it in the manner that led to them being investigated.

With this as the backdrop, City strode into this fevered Anfield atmosphere, with Liverpool fans high on adrenaline and determined to make their contempt for their rivals obvious - then outclassed Andoni Iraola's side in a 3-0 win .

On another day, in other circumstances, the manner of City's victory would have fed the narrative that this was a performance of champions, a winning marker laid down to their rivals as they hold a three-point lead at the top of the table.

Not here. Not in the Premier League's dysfunctional state.

Instead, once the predictable sound and fury had been diluted by City's composure and the swift realisation they were not unnerved by Anfield or the storm raging around the club, this was a surreal experience.

After the feast of excitement delivered when Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp presided over the greatest domestic rivalry of recent years, this was an occasion - remarkable as it seems - that seemed robbed of a sense of jeopardy by the circumstances surrounding it.

Yes, it was a statement display and City celebrated wildly at the final whistle, but will it count for anything given they await potential sanctions suggested including Premier League relegation or a record points deduction?

As Erling Haaland looked close to tears in front of Manchester City 's fans, including his father Alf-Inge, and head coach Enzo Maresca pumped his fists in jubilation, Anfield's DJ slipped Fleetwood Mac's 'Little Lies' on to the loudspeakers in a final message of defiance.

Maresca said: "We knew there was going to be noise but we need to make our own noise by winning games. We need to learn to deal with the noise but the message is to win games.

"For me it's quite easy. I try to focus on things I can control. There are things that are not in my hands so I don't stress about them.

"I cannot control things outside football, so why stress? I stress about gameplan, day-by-day training sessions, but the rest it's not in my hands."

Haaland added: "For every single person part of Manchester City , every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time. It was tough. It was hard, but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone.

"It's always tough to come here. If you look at the record it's tough. With the Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp era it was tough for both teams, always has been. It was important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about. The thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do."

City have appealed against the verdict , but until the dust settles and final decisions are made, this Premier League season is in a holding pattern.

When City come to Anfield and win, especially as convincingly as they did here, it should be a win without qualification or questions.

This does not apply amid the current uncertainty.

Every victory, every league table, will come with a metaphorical asterisk until clarity and finality comes. No-one knows when this will be.

City's players did their jobs to perfection, victory secured by second-half goals from Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki. It is all they can do.

There can be no escape, however, from the cloud hanging over Manchester City because every win will carry the same rider - producing a state of inertia that is not good for the Premier League.

In the end, a day that promised huge discomfort for City ended in a stroll.

City navigated the hostile reception awaiting them at Anfield by arriving through the staff and contractors' entrance - while an inevitable febrile environment awaited them.

Even the derided half-and-half scarves were doing a roaring trade, until it was noticed the sky blue half read: 'Shamchester City - The Cheats'.

The announcement of City's line-up was drowned out by deafening jeers, while banners around Anfield carried a variety of messages.

They including 'A Generation Of Supporters Cheated', 'And After All You Really Robbed Us All' and - in a nod to the Oasis song Stop Crying Your Heart Out, written by Noel Gallagher who was at Anfield, 'All Of Your Stars Are Fading Away'.

This was all watched by an impassive City chief executive Ferran Soriano, but any notion their fans would turn on the owners was dispelled by a flag reading: 'In Khaldoon We Trust. We've Won It All', a gesture of support for the embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

City's fans also waved hundreds of inflatable bananas, an old habit when they spent time in the lower leagues in reduced circumstances. There remains the possibility they will get the chance to wave them down the tiers once more in the near future.

The first half did much to pour cold water on what started as a red-hot atmosphere, further diluted by City's second-half domination, although Liverpool 's fans rammed home their disgust until the final whistle, chanting "cheat" every time their opponents passed in a lengthy period of possession.

Former Liverpool and England defender Stephen Warnock told BBC Radio 5 Live: "This needs rectifying as quickly as possible, but this isn't an easy thing to come to a conclusion. It's never-ending. It's so difficult and it's going to take so long to sort out."

He added: "The hard part is that this is a brilliant Manchester City team, but you have to caveat it and say they have done it illegally and they bought their way. You're caught in what you're thinking about this City team.

"I admire them because they're so good individually and so great, but the way it has been done and put together has not been put together correctly."

While ex-Man Utd striker Wayne Rooney, added: "I know what it is like from managing Derby County when they had a points deduction. The mindset and message to the players was simple – just try to win the next game.

"All the noise around the club, from the media and other fans, will make them even hungrier to succeed.

"They could be fighting for the title or fighting for relegation by the end of the season. Who knows what's going to happen."

As City walked off, they were accompanied by the taunt of "You're going down" from the Kop.

City's fans answered with the trademark: "We're not really here."

This, in essence, is what makes this Premier League campaign one that might yet be rendered void. City might win the title - but who knows if they will be here next season?

As Maresca's side move into top gear and threaten to accelerate away from the chasing pack with wins such as this, no-one has a clue what their final destination will be.

articles.title: Raba resucita de la mano de Aguirre tras más de un año 'olvidado'
articles.standfirst: En el último año natural había jugado 88 minutos de Liga y con el mexicano debutó como titular y marcó antes del minuto dos de partido
articles.summary: En el último año natural había jugado 88 minutos de Liga y con el mexicano debutó como titular y marcó antes del minuto dos de partido
articles.body: Los cambios de entrenador suelen traer situaciones nuevas en los equipos, pero lo de Dani Raba con el 'vasco' Aguirre es de premio. El atacante, que desde hace más de un año era un jugador desaparecido y olvidado fue titular en el primer partido del mexicano y tardó menos de 100 segundos en marcar. Una resurrección exprés que podría cambiar su rol en el equipo de forma radical. Un gol que no celebró al hacerlo contra el club de su formación y que mostró todos sus recursos con recorte y definición de mucha calidad. Lo de Dani Raba desde que desembarcó en el Valencia, llegó el verano pasado libre de contrato procedente del Leganés, ha sido una tortura. Fue titular en el primer partido de la pasada campaña con Corberán, repitió cuatro jornadas después en el once y nunca más había vuelto a saltar de inicio. Más de un año viendo el fútbol desde el banquillo y participando de forma residual. En un año natural Raba no ha llegado a los cien minutos repartidos en diez encuentros. El resto de partidos no pasó del calentamiento. Esta misma campaña su aportación fueron ocho minutos ante el Deportivo cuando el encuentro estaba ya perdido. De hecho, el club presionó de forma evidente y repetida al jugador para que buscara una salida en verano, pero el futbolista, con dos años de contrato por delante, decidió que no era el momento de marcharse y su suerte puede haber cambiado. Algo debe haber visto Aguirre en sus primeros días en Valencia para darle la titularidad y el delantero ha respondido con un gol casi sin tiempo para que nadie pusiera en duda su alineación. El cántabro valoró su regreso a los terrenos de juego como titular en el debut de Aguirre en el banquillo. "Estoy contento con volver a jugar, a partir de ahora vamos a ver otro Valencia. Hemos tenido poco tiempo para trabajar y poco a poco vamos a mejorar. He visto que el defensa se me cruzaba y he sabido esperar y ha sido lo mejor para el equipo".

articles.title: Man City's Elliot Anderson deemed a bargain while Florian Wirtz fails to offer return on Liverpool's huge investment - Premier League hits and misses
articles.summary: Sky Sports' football writers analyse Sunday's Premier League action as Florian Wirtz shrinks on the big occasion again, but Elliot Anderson shines; Crystal Palace spoil Oliver Glasner's Selhurst Park return; Everton missing clinical edge to become European contenders
articles.body:
Manchester City's siege mentality won out at Liverpool. Their quality with a man over telling, if not quite so obvious when both sides had a full complement of players for an hour of the game.

Absolutely everything good about City in their 3-0 win was summed up by the classy performance of Elliot Anderson.

Not for the first time since his mega-money move from Nottingham Forest, the midfielder's mastery on the ball was matched by his maturity off it. A "bargain" at £116m, according to Jamie Carragher, every bit capable, in his own way, of exerting as much control and influence on games as Rodri did in this role.

While the spotlight shines ever brighter on City as a club, and forensics pour over their spending, Anderson remains the picture of calm. Everything a manager would want in a modern-day holding midfielder: a robust runner, aggressive tackler and clever distributor. "He dominates big games," says Gary Neville.

Rarely fazed by the occasion, Anderson has won at Anfield two years running - with two different sides. Of course the way Forest went about success last term shared few similarities with City's more technical display. The only common denominator? Elliot Anderson. Laura Hunter

Florian Wirtz played his part with the pressing and the constant movement that was a hallmark of Liverpool's up-tempo approach that made life so difficult for Manchester City for an hour at Anfield. But that bit of magic that the supporters wanted was missing.

Rayan Cherki provided that for City's third and final goal, by which point Wirtz was sat on the Liverpool bench having been substituted. Another big game in which the Germany international was unable to provide the spark for his side.

Too many loose touches and loose passes, one or two tackles shirked. Victor Munoz and Lewis Koumas are easy for supporters to embrace with their bustling styles but Wirtz is a player who glides across the turf and he needs end product to justify his role.

There was one shot lashed wide with the game goalless and better options to his left. It is no goals for Wirtz this season and just one in his last 16 Premier League appearances. Another opportunity missed for a classy player still seemingly unable to impose himself. Adam Bate

Crystal Palace have shown signs of rediscovering their attacking spark under Pierre Sage, with their 3-1 comeback win over Nottingham Forest the latest example.

The Eagles have now scored three or more goals in two of their last four league games - as often as they managed across their previous 37 Premier League matches combined.

Goals and entertaining football were a problem during Oliver Glasner's latter days in charge, as Palace struggled to balance their domestic and European commitments.

There is an early sense of a throwback to the more free-scoring side that flourished under the Austrian in his first season, when their pace, movement and attacking combinations made them a threat to anyone.

It is still early in Sage's tenure, and two high-scoring performances do not guarantee a lasting change. But Palace look to be playing with greater freedom and confidence, with Daichi Kamada, Jefferson Lerma and Yeremy Pino all finding the net against Forest.

If Sage can sustain that attacking momentum while tightening up a defence that has been vulnerable this season, there are encouraging signs of a more dangerous Palace taking shape. William Bitibiri

Everton are unbeaten after six matches for just the third time in the Premier League era. In 2006/07 and 2013/14 they finished sixth and then fifth from this position.

It is a testament to the hard work of David Moyes, who has returned to challenging circumstances in his second Everton spell, that he has got the club back to looking upwards.

For the last five seasons, Everton have been in the bottom half, often battling relegation. Now, it seems, they have a genuine chance to push up the table and dare to dream bigger.

However, it is hard to see how Moyes can drag them into Europe with Thierno Barry as his only striker. The 23-year-old scored in the end in the 2-2 draw at Hull, but, according to Opta, he needed five big chances to find the back of the net. At least two of those had to go in.

If Everton are to qualify for Europe, they will need a striker who wins them points. At Hull, you could argue they had a striker who cost them points.

Barry, who is Everton's top scorer since the start of last season in the Premier League (11 goals), is improving all the time, but the current situation is unfair on him and his manager. Right now he cannot be depended on consistently.

The Frenchman, who has started all eight of Everton's matches this season, appeared to pull up with cramp towards the end at Hull and Moyes had no choice but to replace him with Charly Alcaraz, who is a midfielder by trade.

There was only four minutes plus stoppage time to go, but it almost felt as if Everton were forced to give up on chasing a late winner. This was a match that was there for the taking.

The plan, of course, was to have Folarin Balogun in the squad. However, his move from Monaco collapsed at the last minute on Deadline Day.

The obvious solution would be to go back in for a striker in January. It remains to be seen how the uncertainty at ownership level will impact their plans. Moyes needs - and deserves - another striker to have a proper chance at a push for Europe. Zinny Boswell

Mohamed Belloumi is making the difference for Hull City - even when he is tired.

The Algeria winger was benched for the first time this season against Everton after telling head coach Sergej Jakirovic on Friday that he was fatigued after playing three times for his country during the international break.

Belloumi still made a crucial impact on Sunday, netting Hull's equaliser to earn them a point. He has been pivotal in the club's good start, scoring or assisting five of their eight Premier League goals this season.

The 24-year-old was signed from Portuguese side Farense in August 2024 and scored only five goals in 35 Championship appearances over two seasons, but, at a higher level, his pace and fearless dribbling has made a significant contribution already.

Belloumi will return to being the first name on their teamsheet at Fulham next weekend and, if his early-season form is anything to go by, defences will have plenty more to worry about. David Richardson

articles.title: Why did Man City fans bring 1,000 balloon BANANAS to Anfield? The bizarre 1980s story behind their defiant display during 3-0 win over angry Reds
articles.summary: Discover the quirky tradition of Manchester City fans bringing inflatable bananas to Anfield during their match against Liverpool, and learn about the bizarre origins of this colorful spectacle.
articles.body: Manchester City arrived at Anfield expecting hostility, with Liverpool supporters ready to make their feelings known after the Premier League’s verdict against their rivals. Yet amid the boos, banners and talk of a potentially fiery afternoon, the travelling City fans had a rather different response: hundreds of inflatable bananas, reviving one of English football’s strangest traditions. By full-time, City had won 3-0, stayed top of the Premier League and given their supporters plenty to celebrate.City silence Anfield as Haaland and Doku take controlErling Haaland had promised business as usual ahead of Manchester City’s first match since the financial verdict, and his team delivered precisely that, winning their sixth consecutive league game. The build-up suggested an afternoon dominated by hostility towards the visitors, but Enzo Maresca’s side eventually turned the occasion into another emphatic result.City were booed by the home crowd during their warm-up, while Liverpool supporters made their position clear with banners featuring the word “CHEAT” and another reading, “Look back in anger, Shamchester.” Reports also described discussions about a hostile reception for the visiting team bus, prompting Merseyside Police to confirm a security operation around the match.Maresca had insisted his players could handle the pressure, drawing on the experience of footballers accustomed to hostile stadiums. “Absolutely, [the City players] can face the pressure,” he said before the match. “We have players who have experience of similar situations. Enzo Fernandez played in Argentina. In Argentina, almost every game is like you go to Anfield.”The atmosphere was intense, but the match shifted decisively after Liverpool midfielder Ryan Gravenberch received a second yellow card and was sent off shortly after the hour mark. City took advantage of their numerical superiority, with Haaland opening the scoring four minutes later before Jérémy Doku struck three minutes afterwards, bending the ball into the top corner after making a decisive impact from the bench.Rayan Cherki added the third goal as City completed a 3-0 victory that kept them at the top of the table. Haaland’s finish, his eighth goal in seven City games this season according to the match report, came after he reacted quicker than Liverpool’s defenders inside the box, allowing him to celebrate in front of his father, Alf-Inge Haaland.Doku’s influence extended beyond his goal, as his direct approach helped provoke the challenge that led to Gravenberch’s dismissal. Noel Gallagher was among the familiar faces watching from the stands, while Haaland’s father also attended, giving the visiting contingent plenty to enjoy beyond the defiant display of yellow inflatables.The financial verdict that set the stage for AnfieldThe hostility surrounding City had been building since an independent commission found the club guilty of 114 out of 115 Premier League financial and cooperation charges on September 29, covering alleged breaches connected to the period between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons. City denied the allegations and subsequently filed an appeal, while the potential sanctions remained undecided.Liverpool supporters used the occasion to make their views known, turning the banners and chants into a public response to the case. City’s travelling fans, however, brought their own statement of defiance, choosing an old club tradition rather than answering every taunt directlyDante Friend, associated with the City supporters’ group 1894, told Sporting News: “The message is obviously defiance. We don’t give a f*** who the owners are, we are the club. The fans are the club.”That attitude helped explain why the inflatable bananas mattered beyond their comic appearance, particularly on a day when the team’s relationship with its ownership and the consequences of the financial case were under intense scrutiny.Why Manchester City fans bring inflatable bananasThe tradition dates back to the 1987-88 season, when Manchester City returned to Division Two after relegation from the top division the previous year. Its origins had little to do with protests, financial allegations or elaborate displays of support, beginning instead with a nickname that was almost too silly not to catch on.Former City forward Imre Varadi became the subject of a pun when one supporter referred to him as “Imre Banana”. According to Dante Friend, a fan named Frank Newton then brought an inflatable banana to the following match, prompting others to follow his lead until the fruit became an unmistakable part of the club’s fan culture.The novelty was not confined to bananas, as supporters experimented with other inflatable objects, including paddling pools, fried eggs and Frankenstein’s monster. The bananas, however, proved the most enduring, becoming an instantly recognisable symbol of Manchester City’s following during a period when the club’s fortunes on the pitch were far less impressive than they are today.Varadi played for several English clubs during his career, including Everton, Sheffield Wednesday and Leeds United, but his association with City gave him an unusually lasting place in the club’s folklore. He scored 31 goals in 81 appearances for City across all competitions, although the nickname inspired by him would become one of the more memorable parts of his footballing legacy.The tradition gradually faded over the years, making its appearance at Anfield particularly striking. Supporters’ group 1894 organised a revival for the Liverpool trip, distributing upwards of 1,000 inflatable bananas among travelling fans, many of whom gathered in the left-hand corner of the Anfield Road End.Varadi himself joined in with the joke on social media, writing on X: “The bananas are taking over Anfield!” He added that City fans were ready to party at Liverpool, neatly capturing the spirit of a ritual that had outlived its original pun by nearly four decades.By the end of the afternoon, the bananas had offered Manchester City supporters a memorable way to answer a hostile reception, while their team supplied the result that made the display even sweeter. The financial case will continue beyond this match, but at Anfield, City left with three points, six league wins from six and a revival of one of football’s most delightfully peculiar traditions.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: El Sporting enfría al Cádiz en el último suspiro con algo de fortuna
articles.standfirst: Un disparo de Pablo García que desvía ligeramente Manu en el tramo final le da tres puntos de oro al conjunto asturiano
articles.summary: Los asturianos no ganaban en la Tacita de Plata desde 2008
articles.body: Con un gol algo afortunado de Pablo García en la recta final el Sporting doblega al Cádiz, donde no ganaba desde el año 2008, tras un partido bastante igualado y se lleva la victoria de la Tacita de Plata con lo que suma su tercera victoria a domicilio en cuatro salidas y asalta provisionalmente la zona de 'playoffs'. Los amarillos, que dispusieron de las mejores ocasiones antes del descanso, no pueden dar continuidad a su primer triunfo y seguirán una semana más en descenso. Celades introdujo una única modificación en el once, con Moueffek por Doué, y el Sporting dominó los primeros compases sin generar demasiado peligro, aunque David Gil tuvo que resolver una internada de Gaspar Campos. Las oportunidades más claras fueron locales. Dilan Zárate encontró la carrera de Sergio Arribas, que no acertó con su vaselina ante Rubén Yáñez. A la media hora Ibon Sánchez mandó por encima del larguero una dejada de Vladys tras gran acción de Antoñito Cordero. Y antes del descanso, Moueffek tampoco conectó otro centro de Vladys cuando estaba en una posición favorable para marcar. Para el cuadro asturiano la tuvo Gelabert, que remató en el área pequeña un gran centro de Gularte, pero David Gil le respondió con un paradón. El Cádiz quiso asumir la iniciativa en la segunda mitad, pero encontró dificultades para generar ocasiones y aprovechar sus transiciones. Doué sustituyó a Moueffek y, en el minuto 65, Cordero probó a un seguro Rubén Yáñez con un disparo con la zurda. El Sporting fue asentándose con el paso de los minutos, mientras los amarillos llegaban cada vez más incómodos y con menos frescura al desenlace. Así, en la recta final, Pablo García aprovechó una desconexión defensiva para marcar el único gol, con un disparo dentro del área que desvió ligeramente Manu Fernández, decantando la balanza a favor del Sporting. Un golpe que el Cádiz ya no pudo contrarrestar y que llevó la alegría a la marea rojiblanca que acompañó a los suyos en el sur peninsular. Los de Larcamón suman así su segunda victoria consecutiva y dejan a los de Celades en puestos de descenso una semana más.

articles.title: El efecto Aguirre se queda a medias
articles.standfirst: El Valencia saca un punto de El Sardinero
articles.summary: El Valencia saca un punto de El Sardinero
articles.body: El efecto Aguirre se queda a medias. El Valencia solo pudo sacar un empate de El Sardinero ante un buen Racing, en el estreno del técnico mexicano en el banquillo valencianista. Pudo llevarse los tres puntos (Hugo Duro falló un gol cantado en la última jugada del partido), pero también es cierto que pudo irse de vacío. Al final un reparto de puntos que hace justicia con los méritos de uno y otro equipo, pero que no deja satisfecho a ninguno. Fue una de las novedades en el primer once de Javier Aguirre con el Valencia. Dani Raba, que solo había disputado ocho minutos esta temporada, disfrutaba de su primera titularidad y el cántabro tardó dos minutos en marcar el 0-1. Pidió perdón por haber marcado al equipo de su tierra, pero el extremo valencianista no podía disimular su felicidad por el tanto anotado. La jugada se gestó en un saque de banda a favor del Racing que recupera inmediatamente el Valencia. Hugo Duro bloquea a Pablo Ramón y deja vía libre para Raba, que recorta a Belocian y a Prati antes de batir a Agirrezabala. Un gran gol que, sin embargo, no dio el impulso necesario al Valencia para gobernar el partido. El Racing reaccionó y comenzó a jugar al fútbol y a hacerlo bien. Es lo normal teniendo a jugadores como Canales, Almeida, Iñigo Vicente e Iván Martín en la zona de creación. Todos ellos hablan el mismo idioma futbolístico y la calidad se les cae de los bolsillos. A estos hay que sumarles el alto nivel de juego que está mostrando Zabiri en este inicio de temporada. El Racing, siempre que tiene opción, elige correr, jugando al primer toque y buscando desplazamientos de balón verticales que rompan las líneas del rival. Así llegó el tanto del empate. Iñigo Vicente metió un pase de tiralíneas a la espalda de De Haas, Zabiri lo controló y sacó un zapatazo con el interior de su pie derecho que se coló por el palo corto de Dimitrievski. Del Valencia, al margen del gol, solo inquietó la meta racinguista con un cabezazo de Gayà y una volea de Javi Guerra. En ambos casos la bola se marchó rozando el palo. Aguirre movió el banquillo tras el descanso, dando entrada a Danjuma por Diakhaby y buscando algo más de presencia ofensiva de su equipo, pero a los dos minutos de la reanudación Iván Martín daba la vuelta al marcador con un remate desde la frontal ajustado al palo. Pudo empeorar la cosa para el Valencia poco después, cuando el árbitro le perdonó la segunda amarilla a Guido por un agarrón clamoroso sobre Salinas. Reaccionó el Valencia y, tras un par de llegadas infructuosas, Otorbi, que llevaba apenas 10 minutos sobre el terreno de juego, restablecía el empate. El Valencia seguía insistiendo y Otorbi volvía a tener una grandísima oportunidad de marcar que salvó Belocian despejando a córner con Agirrezabala ya batido. El central del Racing volvió a ser protagonista, pero esta vez en el área contraria, cabeceando un balón a las manos de Dimitrievski. El defensa se había sumado al ataque en una jugada a balón parado. El meta valencianista también se lució ante un remate desde cerca de Andrés Martín y, ya en la prolongación, sacando una mano salvadora a un remate de Pablo García. Luego llegó la clarísima oportunidad de Hugo Duro tras una buena cabalgada de Otorbi por la derecha que el delantero remató fuera. Ahí tuvo el triunfo el Valencia.

articles.title: Mourinho, contra el incendio que amenaza al Madrid
articles.standfirst: Quiere evitar que la indignación arbitral, las protestas y la expulsión de Vini terminen pasando factura
articles.summary: Quiere evitar que la indignación arbitral, las protestas y la expulsión de Vini terminen pasando factura
articles.body: El Real Madrid ganó al Villarreal, pero el partido dejó mucho más que tres puntos. La expulsión de Vinicius, las protestas de Mourinho y de todo el banquillo, la tensión acumulada sobre el césped y un balance disciplinario de seis amarillas y una roja para el conjunto blanco dibujaron un escenario que el técnico portugués quiere evitar a toda costa... para que la indignación termine convirtiéndose en un problema para su propio equipo. Mourinho acabó el encuentro con un enfado de época. El portugués pasó de celebrar junto a Vinicius el gol que habría supuesto el 2-0 a llevarse las manos a la cabeza cuando el VAR anuló la acción y el brasileño terminó expulsado. A partir de ese momento, el partido entró en una dinámica de máxima tensión. Las protestas se multiplicaron, el banquillo elevó el tono y el Madrid tuvo que resistir con diez jugadores: "Si en cada acción estás pidiendo algo... El árbitro es un ser humano y puede entrar en algún error", explicó Foyth tras el partido. La imagen más significativa llegó después del pitido final. Mourinho decidió no comparecer ante los medios, una decisión que, según pudo saber MARCA, buscaba evitar unas declaraciones que pudieran exponerlo a una sanción y comprometer su presencia en el Clásico. El entrenador optó por el silencio en lugar de alimentar una polémica que seguía muy presente tras el partido. En el vestuario, la victoria no borró el malestar. La sensación de injusticia por algunas decisiones arbitrales convivió con el alivio de haber sumado tres puntos importantes. Sin embargo, Mourinho sabe que el enfado, por comprensible que resulte para sus jugadores, también puede convertirse en un arma de doble filo si termina condicionando su comportamiento y su rendimiento. La expulsión de Vinicius es el mejor ejemplo de las consecuencias que puede dejar una noche así. El brasileño pidió disculpas a sus compañeros y a la afición, pero la redacción del acta arbitral abre la puerta a una sanción que podría dejarlo fuera de compromisos importantes. Es precisamente ese escenario el que Mourinho quiere evitar. El portugués no pretende que el equipo olvide lo sucedido ni que el malestar desaparezca de un día para otro. Quiere que los jugadores sean capaces de canalizarlo sin perder la concentración, evitando que las protestas, las tarjetas y las reacciones en caliente acaben teniendo más peso que el fútbol. Porque el riesgo va más allá de un arbitraje discutido o de una expulsión. Con una temporada exigente por delante y partidos decisivos en el horizonte, el Madrid no puede permitirse que cada episodio polémico lo arrastre a una espiral de tensión, sanciones y desgaste. La cuestión arbitral queda en manos de Mourinho y de los dirigentes del club; la respuesta del equipo debe darse sobre el terreno de juego. Y es que la idea es clara y el portugués no quiere que la polémica se lleve por delante al equipo.

articles.title: Aguirre: "A Otorbi y a Raba no los conocía de nada"
articles.standfirst: El técnico mexicano considera justo el empate el partido de su debut al frene del Valencia
articles.summary: El técnico mexicano considera justo el empate el partido de su debut al frene del Valencia
articles.body: Javier Aguirre celebró un punto en el día de su debut con el Valencia. El mexicano fue muy realista a la hora de valorar el partido y aseguró que el empate fue justo. "Yo creo que es justo el empate. Hubiera sido una injusticia el gol en el añadido de Hugo Duro para ellos. Creo que estuvimos serios y solidarios. Los cambios nos dieron muchas cosas y pudimos sumar algo más, estuvimos cerca, pero creo que el resultado es justo" El nuevo entrenador del Valencia lanzó flores al rival por el nivel mostrado sobre el campo. "El Racing es un equipo muy bueno que vinieron como aviones, debo felicitar al míster rival por lo que han mostrado sobre el campo. Además han contado con una afición que apretaba mucho". Aguirre destacó los momentos en los que el Valencia pareció desconectar del partido y que le costaron que el Racing pudiera remontar. "Dimos en ocasiones alguna sensación de fragilidad. Nos falta algo de trabajo, hemos trabajado, pero nos falta. Hemos recuperado la energía y las ganas de jugar. Vimos un equipo sólido y solidario y que siempre va a competir. Por último, el mexicano dejó una de esas frases de su repertorio particular al valorar el partido de Raba y Otrobi, los goleadores del Valencia. "A Otorbi y Raba no los conocía de nada. Cuando me fui de LaLiga no existían. Los vi entrenar y sé que jugaban bien. Raba llevaba más de un año sin marcar e hizo un buen gol, luego poco a poco se le acabó la gasolina". "Tenemos que ser fuertes ahí. En casa, con el cariño y el ánimo de la gente. Sentimos que hay mucha Liga. Somos un equipo que vamos a competir muy bien. Perdimos muy fácil la pelota. El primer pase de seguridad no lo dábamos, la verdad. Pasamos a línea de cuatro, porque estábamos tres contra uno y fue culpa mía por no leer bien el partido. Luego la segunda parte bien. Mejor. Somos un equipo que estábamos encontrándonos. El paso A lo dimos, que es actitud. Con el talento que tenemos haremos mejores partidos". "Lo vi a él, a Raba y a Elliott muy bien desde que llegué. Es verdad que a un 9 se le juzga por los goles, pero trabajó muchísimo. Se le fue el último gol porque no podía con los gemelos. Es lo que tienen los 9, que te fallan una así y luego te meten tres".

articles.title: Big Ten admits its officials made a massive error on Oregon's game-tying 2-point conversion attempt in loss vs. UCLA
articles.summary: The Ducks should have snapped the ball inside the 1-yard line. Instead, they snapped it a yard further back.
articles.body:
Oregon fans have a legitimate case that an officiating mistake cost the Ducks a real chance at stealing a win over UCLA.

The Bruins knocked off Oregon 17-15 on Saturday after stopping Oregon's game-tying 2-point conversion with 2:16 to go. However, the Big Ten admitted that Oregon should have snapped the ball closer to the end zone on Jordon Davison's run.

"Following the first attempt that resulted in a personal foul penalty for a facemark on the UCLA defense, the ball was spotted for the second attempt half-the-distance to the goal from the original line of scrimmage of the first attempt," the conference's statement said. "Per rule, the ball should have been spotted half-the-distance to the goal from the end of the run of the first attempt."

UCLA stopped Davison's run after the ball was snapped halfway from the 3-yard line, or the original line of scrimmage where Oregon first attempted its initial 2-point conversion. However, the Ducks got to the 1-yard line on the initial attempt, meaning it should have only needed a half-yard to get the game tied.

It's an incredibly huge error in a game that could very well cost Oregon a chance at the College Football Playoff.

The Ducks are now 3-2 and may need to win out to have a chance at the postseason. Oregon still has a game against No. 4 Ohio State remaining, too.

However, Oregon shouldn't be in a position of blaming the officials for the loss.

This is a team that committed seven turnovers when you count the recovered fumble on the final last-ditch play of the game. And Oregon shouldn't have needed to go for two to begin with. After UCLA took an early 3-0 lead, Oregon coach Dan Lanning went for two after the Ducks' first touchdown.

That failed. Oregon led 6-3 instead of 7-3. Two made extra points would have meant the game was tied at 17-17 just before the two-minute warning.

The Big Ten's year of officiating errors marches on

One thing is for certain, however. The Big Ten has got to get its officiating issues sorted out.

This is at least the third issue from a Big Ten game so far this season. By now, everyone knows about the one-second debacle at the end of Michigan's 13-12 win over Western Michigan in Week 1 when Big Ten officials added one second back to the clock ahead of the Wolverines' game-winning Hail Mary.

While the Big Ten said it was utilizing the game clock to make that timing determination, it also didn't follow the timing protocols in the replay handbook when adding the second back. Had the manual's protocols been followed, Western Michigan would have won.

In Week 5, that same Big Ten officiating crew denied Nebraska the chance to re-attempt a missed extra point after a Maryland penalty in the Huskers' 25-point win. Officials instead assessed the penalty on the ensuing kickoff. Nebraska coach Matt Rhule took the blame after the Big Ten's statement, though he said that he was informed by a member of the officiating crew that the PAT had been made when asked if he wanted to accept the penalty on the kickoff.
